summary: Evening burst: reserved pool throughput collapse due to autoscale undershoot and tenant GPU monopolization
description: Issue summary: During the customer's evening traffic spike (approx 19:00–20:30 local), the dedicated reserved GPU pool servicing HelixDocs experienced a ~60% drop in sustained throughput and elevated p95/p99 latencies accompanied by intermittent request timeouts (504). Impact: HelixDocs reported degraded user experience across document-summarization endpoints; several production customers timed out and opened support channels. Environment: Dedicated reservation (pool-helix-001) in prod-us-east-1 using pinned redwood-open-7b-v2. Expected behavior: Pool autoscaler should scale to meet the concurrent request load and preserve p95 latency under the target SLO. Observed: slow/insufficient scale-up, repeated GPU context thrashing, and single-tenant batch job monopolization leading to head-of-line queueing.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send synthetic burst traffic matching customer's evening mix: 150 concurrent streaming chat requests plus interleaved 30 long-sequence summarization jobs over 15 minutes.
2) Ensure pool is at min_replicas=2 and autoscaler policies are default cooldown=300s.
3) Observe serving runtime queuing, per-pod GPU utilization, and request latencies via /console/dedicated/pool-helix-001/dashboard.
4) Repeat with a heavy background batch job scheduled (simulate tenant's nightly maintenance job).
logs: 2026-03-12T19:07:02Z pool-helix-001 pod/serve-3 gpu0 util=97% gpu1 util=4% kernelexec=long-batch (suspicious)
2026-03-12T19:09:10Z autoscaler: desired_replicas=6 current=2 reason=cpu_or_gpu_utilization threshold_crossed but cooldown_active=true
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: noisy neighbor (HelixDocs scheduled batch) combined with autoscaler cooldown prevented timely scale-up.
Metric evidence: sustained single-GPU saturation spikes on pod/serve-3 while sibling GPU on same node stayed underutilized — indicates uneven job placement and lack of MIG slice balancing.
Autoscaler behavior: observed desired_replicas increased but actual scale-up delayed due to cooldown and node provisioning lag; min_replicas=2 was insufficient for burst shape.
Routing: customer had model pinned to redwood-open-7b-v2; automatic fallback to smaller variant was disabled by their pin, so no graceful degradation occurred.
Kubernetes scheduler logs show repeated pod evictions and rebindings during 19:05–19:20 window, likely due to preemption from background batch controller.
No evidence of hardware fault; telemetry and node-exporter show stable thermal/power readings.
Comparing to baseline day: peak qps pattern has higher long-sequence jobs during this customer's evening hours (customer usage pattern change not previously flagged).
Related runbook: /confluence/runbooks/dedicated-pool-autoscale-troubleshooting referenced for mitigation steps.
comments: Priya Nair (Support) 2026-03-12: Customer reports increased 504s between 19:05–19:25. Provided sample request IDs and timestamps. Asked for urgent triage.
Diego Marquez (SRE) 2026-03-12: Picked up. Spun up extra nodes manually to stabilize pool; requesting customer logs for scheduled jobs.

HelixDocs (Customer) 2026-03-12: Confirmed a nightly ETL-style summarization run was changed last week to include longer context documents, which aligned with spike. They can throttle or reschedule if needed.

Diego Marquez (SRE) 2026-03-13: Found repeated GPU context switching on node-12; probe suggests our scheduler placed a multi-mig job next to latency-critical pods. Opening scheduler policy follow-up (INT-14202).
Priya Nair (Support) 2026-03-13: Communicated interim workaround to customer (enable model fallback + set per-tenant concurrency cap). Customer applied fallback and saw immediate p95 improvement.
Diego Marquez (SRE) 2026-03-13: Will work with infra to add a short-term autoscale tweak (lower cooldown to 60s for this reservation) and submit change to autoscaler config PR.
root_cause: Combination of (1) a tenant-deployed high-cost batch job that saturated individual GPU slices, (2) an autoscaler policy with a long cooldown and low min_replicas that delayed scale-up, and (3) scheduler placement that left uneven GPU utilization on nodes (MIG slice imbalance). These three factors produced head-of-line queueing and intermittent request timeouts.
resolution: Applied a three-step mitigation: 1) temporarily lowered autoscaler cooldown to 60s and increased desired_replicas cap for pool-helix-001; 2) enabled customer-configured model fallback to a smaller variant to reduce per-request GPU time; 3) isolated nightly batch workload by applying a per-tenant concurrency policy and scheduling window. After changes, p95 returned to SLO within 12 minutes and no new 504s observed.
recommended_followup: 1) Update autoscaler policy: consider dynamic cooldown tied to event type and allow faster scale-up for dedicated reservations with SLOs.
2) Improve scheduler placement: add MIG-awareness and per-tenant isolation heuristics to avoid GPU slice monopolization.
3) Offer customer advisory: detect and notify customers when their usage pattern shifts to heavier long-sequence jobs and recommend model fallback or concurrency caps.
4) Postmortem: complete draft on Confluence and consider opt-in autoscale profile for high-variance customers.
5) Create follow-up internal task to audit reserved pools for min_replicas values that are too low for typical burst shapes (INT-14202).
